short: A brief but incredibly bloody battle where US Marines seized heavily fortified Tarawa Atoll.
full:
From 20 to 23 November 1943, United States Marines launched an assault on the heavily fortified Betio Island in the Tarawa Atoll, marking the beginning of the central Pacific offensive. The Japanese had transformed the tiny island into a formidable fortress, bristling with coastal artillery, machine gun nests, and nearly five thousand elite defenders ordered to fight to the death.

The initial American landings were plagued by exceptionally low tides that stranded landing craft on the coral reefs, forcing Marines to wade ashore under intense fire. Over seventy-six hours of savage, close-quarters combat ensued before the island was secured. Almost the entire Japanese garrison was annihilated, while American forces suffered over three thousand casualties. The staggering losses shocked the American public but provided crucial tactical lessons for future amphibious assaults.
